title: CouncilLens topic model
description: The contract for one council + one topic, written by the analyse stage to data/analysed/<council-slug>/<topic-slug>.json and read by the publish stage. Strict: unknown fields are rejected, so a council-specific field cannot leak into the site.

source_ids.description: Canonical record ids this output was derived from.

review_status.description: needs_review: unchecked. ai_reviewed: independently checked against the source documents by a second AI pass, not yet by a person. reviewed: checked by a person.

reviewed_by.description: Who checked it: a person's name or handle, or a description of the AI review pass; null until checked.

cache_key.description: sha256 over the item key, the sha256 of each source document's extracted text, and the prompt version. See src/analyse/README.md.

measure_side.description: One side of a comparison — what was planned, or what happened. Null where the council has not published that side, which is what makes a grey status automatic.

value.description: The number the rule compares. A string only where the rule compares outcomes rather than quantities (promise-kept-v1 takes done_on_time, done_late, partly_done or not_done). Null where the document gives nothing the rule can use.

display.description: How to show it, already formatted, e.g. '1.03% under', '£5.5m', 'by November 2026'.

unit.description: GBP for money, % for a share, otherwise what is being counted. Null where the value is an outcome word or a date.

measure.description: One scored comparison: the council's own plan or target on one side, its own reported figure on the other, and a published rule in between. The status is COMPUTED by src/analyse/rules.py from target and actual — it is never carried in the cache, and the analyse stage refuses any measure whose rule_id it does not know.

area.description: Which part of the scorecard this belongs to. 'promises' items are collected into the top-level promises array rather than measures.

question.description: The plain-English question this answers, as a resident would ask it.

label.description: Short name for the measure, including the period it covers.

rule_id.description: Which published rule produced the status. Must be one of the rules in src/analyse/rules.py.

rule.description: The rule in one sentence. Written by the build from the rule's own docstring, never from the cache, so the wording on the page is the wording of the code that ran.

status_word.description: The word shown to a reader. Colour is reinforcement; the word is what carries the meaning.

period.description: The period the measure covers, as the council states it, e.g. '2025/26'.

council_caveat.description: The council's own stated reason or context for this result, in its own words where it gave one. Null where it gave none.

evidence.description: One or two plain sentences a 14-year-old can follow, saying where both numbers come from.

source_url.description: Deep link to the document the numbers came from.

date_string.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Null when the record gives no date at all.

remit_note.description: Plain-English note on what this council does and does not control.

status.description: Carried on outcome events. Null on feedback and decision events.

tier.description: confirmed only where the council's own record cites the feedback.

evidence.description: Verbatim quote from the council record, or null.

figures.description: Key numbers about this council and topic, for the at-a-glance panel. Optional: the array is present only when the analyse stage found cached figures. Every figure must trace to a public document.

label.description: Plain-English name for the number, as a resident would say it.

kind.description: What sort of number this is, so the site can format it without knowing the council.

value.description: The number itself. A string only for kind 'date' (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). Null when the document gives a value the site cannot express as a number.

unit.description: GBP for money; otherwise what is being counted or measured, e.g. 'licences', 'responses', 'working days'. Null for dates.

display.description: How to show it, already formatted, e.g. '677', '£585m', '12 weeks'.

period.description: The period the number covers, as the document states it, e.g. '2025/26' or '2025'. Null for a point-in-time figure.

source_url.description: Deep link to the document the number came from.

note.description: One plain sentence of context: the period, and any caveat such as 'proposed, not yet agreed'.

measures.description: The scorecard for this council and topic: money, targets and service measures scored against the council's own plans by a published rule. Optional — the array is present only when the analyse stage found cached measures. Promises live in their own array.

promises.description: Dated commitments the council made in writing, scored against what its own later records say. Same shape as a measure, with area 'promises': target is the commitment and its date, actual is what the later record says. Optional.
